title: Addressing cognitive bias in medical language models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating language models on the BiasMedQA dataset by injecting text prompts that simulate specific clinical cognitive biases (self-diagnosis, recency, confirmation, frequency, status quo, and false consensus) into multiple-choice USMLE medical questions and measuring the resulting reduction in diagnostic accuracy.

Appending bias-inducing statements into clinical case questions indicating that a patient's cultural background favors an incorrect diagnosis (e.g., the use of herbal remedies) and measuring how often the model is swayed into selecting the incorrect answer.
